mainTopic: Clawing (דרוסה) and how to check for it, רב's ruling on a dislocated windpipe, why we do not add to the טריפות, and the new משנה of כשרות
overview: The amud opens by settling a question: a דרוסה (predator's clawing) on either the וושט or the קנה makes the animal a טריפה at any size, because the venom keeps burning. Two stories follow. In each, scholars say a clawed animal only needs checking near the intestines, and someone swears that רב taught the check runs from the skull to the thigh. When ריש לקיש says he does not know who רב is, רבי יוחנן reminds him how great רב was. ריש לקיש then praises רב and quotes his ruling that a windpipe found loose after שחיטה is כשרה. רבי יוחנן says to test it by comparing cuts, and רב נחמן limits רב's rule to a case where the שוחט did not hold the סימנים. The גמרא explains that the משנה's זה הכלל adds seven more טריפות. Two hunter stories show that we do not add new טריפות, since medicine could heal those wounds. A new משנה then lists injuries that leave an animal כשרה. The גמרא opens with רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש arguing over which list is complete, and starts testing their views on רב מתנא's case of a dislocated hip, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How much clawing on the windpipe makes it a טריפה?
steps.stepSummary: A hole of any size in the וושט makes a טריפה, and so does a דרוסה mark of any size. The קנה only becomes טריפה with a hole the size of an איסר. So how big does a דרוסה mark on the קנה have to be?
steps.simpleTranslation: For the gullet, a hole of any size makes the animal a טריפה, and clawing of any size does too. For the windpipe, a hole must be the size of an איסר. For clawing on the windpipe, how much is needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question. Since the gullet and windpipe have different hole sizes, what is the clawing size for the windpipe?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the וושט, the hole rule and the דרוסה rule match: any amount counts. The קנה needs a bigger hole (an איסר) before it is טריפה. So it is unclear whether a דרוסה on the קנה also needs to reach that size, or whether any amount is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal attacked and clawed by a predator
A small coin, used here as a size measure

phrases.english: The gullet: its perforation is with any amount,
phrases.notes: This means a hole of any size in the gullet makes the animal a טריפה.

phrases.english: its clawing is with any amount.
The windpipe: its perforation is at the size of an issar,
its clawing, at how much?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: How big a דרוסה mark on the קנה must be to make the animal a טריפה

steps.title: Both organs become טריפה from clawing of any amount
steps.stepSummary: The same person who asked the question answers it: for both the וושט and the קנה, a דרוסה of any amount makes the animal a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he asked, he answered it himself: for both of them, any amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The person who asked the question now answers it himself. Clawing of any amount makes either organ a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קנה does not get the איסר size for a דרוסה, even though it does for a hole. For clawing, the קנה is treated just like the וושט.

keyTerms.meaning: After he asked the question, he went back and answered it
Both this one and that one

phrases.english: After he raised the question,
he went back and resolved it:
Both this and that, with any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A דרוסה of any amount makes either the וושט or the קנה a טריפה

steps.title: Why any amount: the venom keeps burning
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that the predator's venom keeps burning, so even a tiny clawed spot will not stay tiny.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Its venom keeps on burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why clawing of any size counts, even on the windpipe. The answer is that the predator's venom keeps burning the spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole stays the size it is, so the קנה can have a minimum size for holes. A דרוסה is different because the venom keeps spreading. That is why there is no safe small size for clawing.
steps.whatToRemember: For דרוסה on the וושט or the קנה, any amount makes a טריפה, because the venom keeps burning.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Its venom keeps burning on and on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the answer in step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The predator's venom keeps burning, so even a small mark is dangerous

steps.title: A clawed animal must be checked near the intestines
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא, sitting before רב נחמן, says that a דרוסה needs to be checked in the area near the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא sat before רב נחמן and said: the דרוסה the Sages spoke about needs checking near the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story starts. A scholar says a clawed animal only needs to be checked near the intestines. This sets up רב נחמן's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we learned how much damage counts. Now the question is where on the animal we have to look. This view limits the check to the middle of the body.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta sat
before Rav Nachman, and he was sitting and saying:
The clawed animal that they spoke of
requires inspection opposite the intestines.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A דרוסה is checked only in the area near the intestines

steps.title: רב נחמן swears that רב required a much wider check
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects with an oath: רב taught that the check runs from the כפא to the thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: By God! רב would teach about it, from the כפא to the thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן strongly disagrees. He swears that רב taught that the check covers a much bigger area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן uses רב's teaching to push back against step 4. The check is not only near the intestines but from the כפא to the אטמא. The meaning of כפא is unclear, and the next step works it out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'By God!', an oath showing he is sure
A hollow, a cup-shaped part of the body

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: By God!
Rav would teach regarding it
from the hollow until the thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the narrow area given in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a דרוסה is checked only near the intestines
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב taught a wider area, from the כפא to the thigh

steps.title: What is the כפא? Not the shoulder
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what כפא means. If it meant the shoulder (the hollow of the foreleg), the area to the thigh would just be the area near the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the כפא? If you say it is the hollow of the foreleg, that is the same as opposite the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what כפא means. It rules out the shoulder, because then רב נחמן would not be adding anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the shoulder to the thigh is the belly area. That is exactly what רב יצחק already said. So רב נחמן's objection only makes sense if כפא means something further away.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)
The hollow of the foreleg, the shoulder area
That is the same thing as

phrases.english: What is the hollow?
If we say the hollow of the foreleg,
that is the same as opposite the intestines,
phrases.notes: So רב נחמן would be saying the same thing as רב יצחק, which can't be.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What body part the word כפא refers to

steps.title: The כפא is the skull
steps.stepSummary: The answer: כפא means the hollow of the brain, the skull. The check runs from the head down to the thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, from the hollow of the brain to the thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that כפא means the skull. רב required checking the whole body, from head to thigh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading it this way gives רב's teaching a real point that differs from the narrow view. The check covers the whole animal.

keyTerms.meaning: The hollow of the brain, the skull

steps.whatToRemember: By רב's teaching, a דרוסה is checked from the skull to the thigh, not only near the intestines.

phrases.english: Rather, from the hollow of the brain until the thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct meaning after step 6 ruled out the shoulder
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כפא is the skull, so the check covers the whole body from head to thigh

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say the same narrow rule
steps.stepSummary: When רב חייא בר יוסף went up to ארץ ישראל, he found רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש saying that a דרוסה is checked near the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב חייא בר יוסף went up, he found רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש sitting and saying: the דרוסה they spoke of needs checking near the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story with the same pattern begins. The great scholars of ארץ ישראל hold the narrow view, and this sets up רב חייא בר יוסף's response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the narrow rule comes from רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש themselves. So whether רב's teaching wins now depends on whether these scholars accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: When he went up (from בבל to ארץ ישראל)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי סְלֵיק רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: When Rav Chiyya bar Yosef went up,
phrases.notes: 'Went up' means he moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he found Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish
who were sitting and saying:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרוּסָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ – צְרִיכָה בְּדִיקָה כְּנֶגֶד בְּנֵי מֵעַיִים.
phrases.english: The clawed animal that they spoke of requires inspection opposite the intestines.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A דרוסה is checked only near the intestines (view held in ארץ ישראל)

steps.title: רב חייא בר יוסף swears by רב's wider check
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר יוסף objects with the same oath: רב taught that the check runs from the כפא to the thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: By God! רב would teach about it, from the כפא to the thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר יוסף repeats רב נחמן's objection to the scholars of ארץ ישראל. He says רב required a much wider check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the same words as רב נחמן did in step 5. Now רב's teaching is being brought to רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, which sets up their reaction.

phrases.english: He said to them: By God!

phrases.aramaic: מוֹרֵי בַּהּ רַב מִכַּפָּא וְעַד אַטְמָא.
phrases.english: Rav would teach regarding it from the hollow until the thigh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָאֱלֹהִים! מוֹרֵי בַּהּ רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrow view stated in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש that the check is only near the intestines
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב taught the check runs from the skull to the thigh

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Who is this רב? I don't know him
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש brushes off the challenge. He asks who this רב is and says he does not know him.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: Who is רב, and who is רב? I don't know him!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש rejects the challenge by saying he does not know who רב is. So רב's teaching does not change his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש does not argue with the content of רב's teaching. He simply does not accept an authority he does not know, so the narrow rule stays in place for him.
steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש does not give a reason against רב's teaching. He only says he does not know who רב is, so he will not rely on him.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to him:
Who is Rav, and who is Rav?
And I do not know him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns away the challenge of step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of רב's teaching as a challenge
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ריש לקיש does not know who רב is, so he does not rely on him

steps.title: רבי יוחנן defends רב's greatness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rejects ריש לקיש's dismissal of רב. He reminds him that רב was a top student of רבי and רבי חייא, and was greater than רבי יוחנן himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Don't you remember that student who served רבי and רבי חייא? By God! All the years that student sat among the top students, I had to stand. And who was greater? He was greater in everything.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes back against ריש לקיש's brush-off of רב. He insists that רב was a giant and must be taken seriously.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש tried to ignore רב חייא בר יוסף's challenge by saying he did not know רב. רבי יוחנן cancels that move: רב sat among the leading students while רבי יוחנן stood, so רב's teaching carries real weight.

keyTerms.meaning: Served, learned under a teacher as his student
Sitting, the honored seat of a leading student
Standing, the lower position of a junior student

steps.whyThisMatters: This restores רב's authority. His teaching that a דרוסה must be checked from the skull to the thigh, and the ruling about שמוטה quoted in the next step, are treated as weighty teachings.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And does he not remember
that student who served
the great Rebbi, and Rabbi Chiya?
phrases.notes: "The great רבי" is רבי יהודה הנשיא. "That student" is רב.

phrases.english: By God!
All those years
that that student served while sitting,
phrases.notes: Sitting means he was one of the senior students, who were allowed to sit during learning.

phrases.english: I served while standing,
and who was greater?
He was greater in everything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's dismissal of רב in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: ריש לקיש's attempt to ignore רב's teaching by claiming not to know him
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב was a great and well-known student of רבי and רבי חייא, greater than רבי יוחנן, so he cannot be dismissed

steps.title: ריש לקיש quotes רב's ruling on a dislocated windpipe
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש immediately praises רב and quotes his ruling: a windpipe found dislocated after שחיטה is כשרה, because a dislocated windpipe cannot be slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away ריש לקיש began and said: Indeed, that man is remembered for good, for they said a teaching in his name: If the windpipe is dislocated and the animal is slaughtered, it is כשרה, since a dislocated windpipe cannot be slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש changes his tone and remembers רב for good by quoting a ruling of his. The ruling deals with a windpipe found torn loose after the animal was slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is one of doubt: did the windpipe come loose before the שחיטה, which would make it a טרפה, or after? רב says we can assume it came loose after, because a loose windpipe would slide away from the knife and could not be cut properly.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching that was handed down
Dislocated, a windpipe torn loose from its place

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying a dislocated windpipe is fine. He is saying that if we find one already slaughtered, it must have been cut before it came loose.

phrases.english: Immediately Reish Lakish began and said:
Indeed, that man is remembered for good,
for they said a teaching in his name:
Dislocated and slaughtered — it is kosher,
phrases.notes: We find the windpipe both torn loose and cut, and we don't know which happened first.

phrases.english: since it is impossible for a dislocated windpipe
to be slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: מיד פתח ריש לקיש ואמר ברם זכור אותו האיש לטוב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After being scolded, ריש לקיש honors רב by quoting a new ruling of his.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A windpipe found dislocated after שחיטה is כשרה, because a dislocated windpipe cannot be slaughtered.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says to test by comparing cuts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב's assumption. He says to bring the windpipe and compare the cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: He should bring the windpipe and compare.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different opinion about the dislocated windpipe. Instead of assuming it is כשרה, we should test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that a loose windpipe can sometimes be cut. So we make a new cut in the loose windpipe and compare it to the שחיטה cut: if they look alike, the שחיטה happened after it came loose and the animal is a טרפה; if they look different, the animal is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: And compare, set side by side

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says:
He should bring it and compare.
phrases.notes: He means: make a fresh cut in the loose windpipe and compare it to the שחיטה cut to see if they match.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רב's ruling in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We do not assume the animal is כשרה; we test it by making a new cut and comparing the two cuts.

steps.title: רב נחמן limits רב's rule to when the סימנים were not held
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that רב's rule applies only when the שוחט did not grip the סימנים. If he held them, a loose windpipe can be cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: They only taught this when he did not grip the סימנים. But if he gripped the סימנים and slaughtered, it is possible for a dislocated windpipe to be slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן narrows רב's ruling. He tells us exactly when the reason "a loose windpipe cannot be cut" really works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's reason is that a loose windpipe slips away from the knife. If the שוחט held the סימנים in his hand, it cannot slip away, so it could have been cut while loose, and רב's proof no longer works.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of, a limiting phrase
The windpipe and food pipe that must be cut in שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: רב: a windpipe found loose after שחיטה is כשרה, since a loose windpipe can't be cut. רבי יוחנן: test it by comparing cuts. רב נחמן: רב's rule works only if the שוחט did not hold the סימנים.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: They only taught this
where he did not grip the simanim,
but if he gripped the simanim and slaughtered,
it is possible for a dislocated windpipe
to be slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב נחמן לא שנו אלא שלא תפס בסימנים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רב's ruling from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's rule applies only when the סימנים were not held; if they were held, a dislocated windpipe can be slaughtered, so the proof that it is כשרה fails.

steps.title: What does the rule 'This is the principle' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case the משנה's closing rule, זה הכלל, comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'This is the principle.' What does that come to add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the words זה הכלל from the משנה and asks what new case they include. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A summary rule in a משנה usually signals that more cases are included than were listed. The גמרא wants to know exactly which cases this rule brings in.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the principle (a summary rule in the משנה)
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even after שחיטה

phrases.english: "This is the principle":
phrases.notes: These words come from the משנה: any animal that could not live with such an injury is a טריפה.

phrases.english: What does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after רב נחמן's explanation of רב's ruling about the windpipe.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which cases are included by the summary rule זה הכלל.

steps.title: It includes the seven extra rulings
steps.stepSummary: The rule זה הכלל comes to include the seven rulings of טריפות taught by later sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include the seven rulings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that זה הכלל includes seven extra cases of טריפה that are not written in the משנה's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These seven cases were taught by the אמוראים. The general rule in the משנה is what gives them their basis, even though the משנה did not name them.

phrases.english: It comes to include the seven rulings.
phrases.notes: These are seven extra טריפות taught by later sages, listed earlier in the מסכת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זה הכלל includes the seven rulings of טריפות taught by the אמוראים.

steps.title: The hunters who struck the sciatic nerve
steps.stepSummary: The men of יוסף the hunter killed animals by hitting the גיד הנשה. רבי יהודה בן בתירא ruled that we cannot add to the list of טריפות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The men of יוסף the hunter would hit the sciatic nerve and kill the animal. They came to רבי יהודה בן בתירא. He told them: Can one add to the טריפות? You only have what the חכמים counted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. Hunters saw that a hit to the גיד הנשה killed animals, and asked if such an animal is a טריפה. The sage said no, because it is not on the חכמים' list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though this wound led to death, רבי יהודה בן בתירא held that the list of טריפות is closed. We do not create new טריפות just because we see animals die from an injury.

keyTerms.term: אֵין לְךָ אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁמָּנוּ חֲכָמִים
keyTerms.meaning: You only have what the חכמים counted (the list is closed)

phrases.english: The men of the house of יוסף the hunter
would strike the sciatic nerve and kill the animal.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא,
phrases.english: They came before רבי יהודה בן בתירא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: וְכִי לְהוֹסִיף עַל הַטְּרֵפוֹת יֵשׁ?
phrases.english: He said to them: Can one add to the טריפות?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁמָּנוּ חֲכָמִים!
phrases.english: You have only what the חכמים counted!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי יוֹסֵף רִישְׁבָּא מָחוּ בְּגִידָא נַשְׁיָא וְקָטְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the extra included cases to a story showing that we cannot add new טריפות on our own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal struck in the גיד הנשה is not a טריפה; we cannot add to the list the חכמים counted.

steps.title: The hunters who struck the kidney
steps.stepSummary: A matching story: the men of רב פפא בר אבא the hunter killed animals by hitting the kidney, and רבי אבא gave the same ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא בר אבא the hunter's men would hit the kidney and kill the animal. They came to רבי אבא. He told them: Can one add to the טריפות? You only have what the חכמים counted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second story with the same pattern. This time the wound is in the kidney, and the answer is the same: not a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second story shows the rule is not limited to one body part. Whether it is the גיד הנשה or the kidney, a wound that is not on the list does not make the animal a טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Can one add to the טריפות? (a rhetorical 'no')

phrases.english: רב פפא בר אבא the hunter:
His men would strike the kidney and kill the animal.
They came before רבי אבא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: וְכִי לְהוֹסִיף עַל הַטְּרֵפוֹת יֵשׁ?
phrases.english: He said to them: Can one add to the טריפות?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁמָּנוּ חֲכָמִים!
phrases.english: You have only what the חכמים counted!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא בַּר אַבָּא רִישְׁבָּא, מָחוּ בְּכוּלְיָא וְקָטְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story giving the same ruling for a different body part.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal struck in the kidney is not a טריפה; we cannot add to the list.

steps.title: But we see these animals die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges both rulings: these animals clearly die from the wound, so why are they not טריפות?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we see that it dies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the two stories. If the animal dies from the wound, it seems it should count as a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה is an animal that cannot keep living. The challenge is that what we see seems to contradict the ruling, since these animals do die.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, but surely (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But we see that it dies!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rulings in steps 17 and 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rulings that animals struck in the גיד הנשה or kidney are not טריפות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טריפה is an animal that will die; these animals are seen to die, so they should be טריפות.

steps.title: With medicine, the animal would live
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a tradition: if medicine were spread on these wounds, the animal would survive.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have a tradition that if one spreads medicine on it, it lives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. These wounds can be healed with medicine, so the animal is not a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dying from a wound left untreated is not enough. An animal is a טריפה only if its injury cannot be healed. Since these wounds can be treated, the animals do not count.
steps.whatToRemember: An animal is not a טריפה just because it died from a wound. If the wound could be healed with medicine, it is not a טריפה, and we cannot add to the list the חכמים counted.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that 'it died' means 'it was a טריפה.' The question is whether the injury can be healed, not whether this animal happened to die.

phrases.english: We have a tradition that if one spreads medicine on it,
it lives.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמִירִי דְּאִי בָּדְרִי לַהּ סַמָּא, חַיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the test for טריפה: whether the injury can be healed, not whether the animal died.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any wound that leads to death makes the animal a טריפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wounds that medicine can heal do not make the animal a טריפה, even if untreated animals die from them.

steps.title: New משנה: A Pierced or Cracked Windpipe Is Kosher
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a list of injuries that do not make an animal a טריפה. It starts with the windpipe, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל sets how big the damage may be.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are kosher in an animal: if its windpipe was pierced or cracked. How much can be missing? רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: up to the size of an Italian איסר coin.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, and this one lists the opposite of the last one: injuries that leave the animal kosher. The first case is a damaged windpipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה listed injuries that make an animal טריפה. Here the משנה lists cases that look dangerous but are still כשר. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits the windpipe case: a hole is fine only up to the size of an איסר.

keyTerms.meaning: Was cracked (a crack along its length)
The Italian איסר, a small coin used as a size measure

phrases.english: MISHNAH: And these are kosher in an animal:
If the windpipe was pierced or cracked.
Up to how much can it be missing?
phrases.notes: He means how big a hole the windpipe can have and still be kosher.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Up to the size of the Italian issar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה that balances the earlier list of טריפות with a list of kosher cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pierced or cracked windpipe does not make the animal טריפה. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, missing tissue is allowed up to the size of an איסר.

steps.title: Injuries That Stop Just Short: Skull, Heart, Spine, Liver
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists four injuries that would make the animal a טריפה if they went one step further, but as described they leave it kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the skull was broken but the brain's membrane was not pierced; if the heart was pierced but not into its chamber; if the spine was broken but its cord was not cut; if the liver was removed but an olive-size piece remained, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing kosher cases. Each one is an injury that stops just before the point that would make the animal טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has a clear line. The danger is the membrane of the brain, the chamber of the heart, the spinal cord, or the whole liver. As long as that vital part is not reached, or a כזית of the liver remains, the animal stays כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Its hollow, the inner chamber of the heart

phrases.english: If the skull was broken open
but the membrane of the brain was not pierced,
if the heart was pierced but not into its chamber,
if the spine was broken
but its cord was not cut,
if the liver was removed
and an olive-bulk of it remained.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִפְחֲתָה הַגּוּלְגּוֹלֶת וְלֹא נִיקַּב קְרוּם שֶׁל מוֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of kosher cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An injury that does not reach the vital part (brain membrane, heart chamber, spinal cord), or a liver with a כזית left, leaves the animal כשרה.

steps.title: More Kosher Cases: Stomachs, Removed Organs, Shriveled Lung
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds more kosher cases: two stomachs pierced into each other, a removed spleen, kidneys, lower jaw or womb, and a lung shriveled by natural causes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the המסס and בית הכוסות were pierced one into the other; if the spleen, the kidneys, the lower jaw, or the womb was removed; or if the lung shriveled by the hand of Heaven, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of kosher cases. It names organs whose damage or removal still leaves the animal כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The המסס and בית הכוסות may be pierced into each other and the animal stays כשרה. Some organs, like the spleen and kidneys, can be missing completely. A lung that shriveled חרותה בידי שמים, from natural causes and not from something done to the animal, is also כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shriveled by the hand of Heaven, from natural causes

phrases.english: The omasum and the reticulum,
that were pierced one into the other.
If the spleen was removed, if the kidneys were removed,
if the lower jaw was removed,
if its womb was removed,
and one shriveled by the hand of Heaven.
phrases.notes: The word for the lung is left out, but the משנה means a lung that shriveled on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶמְסֵס וּבֵית הַכּוֹסוֹת, שֶׁנִּיקְּבוּ זֶה לְתוֹךְ זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of kosher cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These stomach, organ and lung cases do not make the animal טריפה.

steps.title: A Skinned Animal: רבי מאיר vs. חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with a מחלוקת about an animal whose hide was stripped off. רבי מאיר says it is kosher, and the חכמים say it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A skinned animal: רבי מאיר rules it kosher, and the חכמים rule it unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with one case that is disputed. רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about an animal whose skin was removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier cases, this one is not agreed on. רבי מאיר holds that a גלודה is כשרה, and the חכמים hold that it is a טריפה and פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose hide was stripped off

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists injuries that leave an animal כשרה: the windpipe up to an איסר, injuries that stop short of the vital part, some stomach and organ cases, and a naturally shriveled lung. The גלודה is disputed.

phrases.english: The skinned animal: Rabbi Meir deems it kosher,
and the Rabbis deem it unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַגְּלוּדָה – רַבִּי מֵאִיר מַכְשִׁיר, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹסְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the משנה with a disputed case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר rules that a גלודה is kosher. The חכמים rule that it is unfit.

steps.title: Which List Is Exact? רבי יוחנן vs. ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the list of טריפות is exact and complete. ריש לקיש says the list of כשרות is exact and complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was stated: רבי יוחנן said, 'These are טריפות' is precise. רבי שמעון בן לקיש said, 'These are kosher' is precise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a dispute about the two משניות. Each אמורא holds that a different one of the two lists is the complete one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the טריפות list is the full list, so any case not on it is כשר, and the kosher list is only examples. For ריש לקיש, the kosher list is the full list, so any case not on it is טריפה, and the טריפות list is only examples.

keyTerms.meaning: Precisely, an exact and complete list
Animals with fatal defects that may not be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: דוקא means this list is the complete one: only the cases on it get its ruling, and anything missing from it gets the opposite ruling. The other list is then just examples.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
Rabbi Yochanan said:
"These are tereifot" is precise,
phrases.notes: He means the first words of the earlier משנה, which listed the טריפות.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
"These are kosher" is precise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's first discussion of the new משנה, comparing it with the earlier one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: the טריפות list is complete. ריש לקיש: the כשרות list is complete.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whichever list is complete decides the ruling for any case the משנה does not mention.

steps.title: What Case Do They Argue About?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a real case where the two views would give different rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical difference the dispute makes. It is setting up the next step, which names a case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side admits that one list is not complete, so it is not yet clear when their views would rule differently. The גמרא wants a real case that is on neither list.

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference behind the dispute in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete case where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש would rule differently.

steps.title: The Case: רב מתנא's Dislocated Hip Joint
steps.stepSummary: They argue about רב מתנא's ruling that an animal is a טריפה if the head of its thigh bone came fully out of its socket.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about רב מתנא's ruling, since רב מתנא said: if the head of the thigh bone came out of its place, the animal is a טריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the dispute is about רב מתנא's ruling. His case of a dislocated hip is not on either list in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנא rules that a dislocated hip makes the animal טריפה, but neither משנה mentions this case. The question now is how each אמורא fits this ruling with his view of which list is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: The head (ball) of the thigh bone, which sits in the hip socket

phrases.english: With regard to the statement of Rav Mattana,
as Rav Mattana said:
This head of the thigh bone
that slipped out of its place makes it a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about how to explain רב מתנא's ruling that a dislocated hip joint makes the animal טריפה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's View: זה הכלל Covers the Hip Case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's explanation begins. The טריפות list is complete because it includes the זה הכלל clause, which brings in extra cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said 'These are טריפות' is precise: the תנא taught the טריפות, and he taught 'This is the general rule'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining how רבי יוחנן fits רב מתנא's case into the complete טריפות list. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טריפות list ends with זה הכלל, which in step 16 was explained as adding further rulings. So for רבי יוחנן the list can be complete and still include רב מתנא's case through that general clause.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule; a clause that brings in more cases
He (the author of the משנה) taught

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
"These are tereifot" is precise,
the tanna taught the tereifot,
and he taught "This is the general rule,"
phrases.notes: This is the closing line of the earlier משנה, which step 16 said brings in additional rulings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵלּוּ טְרֵפוֹת דַּוְקָא, תְּנָא טְרֵפוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts showing how רבי יוחנן accounts for רב מתנא's case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי יוחנן, רב מתנא's case is included in the complete טריפות list through the זה הכלל clause.
